definitions.explanation: The amount that can be held in one hand when gripped. A physical quantity measurement.

definitions.gloss: a small number; a select few; a tiny minority
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, a very small number of people or things out of a larger group. Emphasizes how few they are.

examples.japanese: {砂|すな}を{一握|ひとにぎ}りつかんだ。
examples.english: I grabbed a handful of sand.

examples.japanese: {塩|しお}を{一握|ひとにぎ}り{入|い}れる。
{米|こめ}を{一握|ひとにぎ}り{鍋|なべ}に{加|くわ}えた。
examples.english: I added a handful of rice to the pot.

examples.japanese: {成功|せいこう}するのは{一握|ひとにぎ}りの{人|ひと}だけだ。
examples.english: Only a handful of people succeed.

examples.japanese: {一握|ひとにぎ}りの{富裕層|ふゆうそう}が{富|とみ}を{独占|どくせん}している。
examples.english: A tiny minority of wealthy people monopolize the wealth.

examples.japanese: その{試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}できるのは、{受験者|じゅけんしゃ}の{中|なか}でもほんの{一握|ひとにぎ}りだ。
examples.english: Among the test takers, only a mere handful can pass that exam.

notes:
{一握|ひとにぎ}り literally means "one grip" — the amount you can hold in a fist. The figurative sense (a tiny minority) is more common in everyday usage.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一握|ひとにぎ}りの{人|ひと}: a handful of people
- {一握|ひとにぎ}りの{企業|きぎょう}: a handful of companies
- ほんの{一握|ひとにぎ}り: a mere handful

RELATED QUANTITY WORDS:
- ひとつかみ: a grab, a handful (similar to {一握|ひとにぎ}り)
- ひとつまみ: a pinch (smaller amount)

WATCH OUT:
Do not confuse with おにぎり ({御握|おにぎ}り), which means rice ball.
